text:
Marisa (AE): Quick sync — Acme POC prompt inventory + success criteria. Customer expects 3 flows (support triage, order summarization, upsell nudges). Timeline: 4 weeks. Who can own baseline prompts + evals?

Priya (SalesEng): I can coordinate with Acme PMs and collect the initial prompt set today. Need placeholder success metrics from Eng/ML to share with them.

Sam (Eng): I can own infra/perf SLOs. Baseline goals we usually propose: latency p95 < 450ms, initial throughput target ~80 req/sec, and cost target < target TBD based on token distribution.

Liam (ML Eng): For quality: propose F1 >= 0.78 on entity extraction tasks, and hallucination rate < 5% on a golden set. Recommend ~200 eval prompts per flow (so ~600 total) for statistical stability.

Anya (Solutions Eng): I’ll draft prompt bundles and quick prompt-engineering notes. Example baseline prompt (first-pass):
```
System: You are a helpful customer support assistant.
User: "My order #12345 hasn't arrived and tracking says 'in transit' for 10 days.'"
Assistant: Provide: 1) likely issue summary, 2) next steps for the user, 3) a suggested escalation label for the support ticket.
```
Keep prompts terse to minimize token variance.

Jen (Pricing): Quick pricing question — do we know hosted vs dedicated for Acme? Hosted = usage-based (estimate ranges depend on tokens & throughput), Dedicated = reserved capacity + commit (starts materially higher but predictable). We should get a signal from procurement — if they want predictable p50 cost, we push Dedicated conversation.

Noel (Security): Security checklist: SOC2, SSO (SAML/SCIM), IP allowlisting, encryption at rest/in-transit, retention controls, and a completed security questionnaire. Can Marisa drop their questionnaire here? Also: EU data residency is often brought up.

Marisa (AE): I’ll get the security questionnaire PDF from Acme and confirm hosting preference. Current blockers: legal review on the MSA, SSO onboarding window, and sample data sharing (they're tight on live PII). @Noel can you take point on the questionnaire?

Noel (Security): Assigning to me. Also flag: Acme prefers EU-only data residency for production — we may need Private deployment or Dedicated in EU region.

Sam (Eng): Model plan: start with a Redwood-verified open model quantized variant for baseline runs (cost-friendly) and add a higher-capacity hosted model as fallback for edge-case generation. We'll need kernel/quant config for latency targets.

Liam (ML Eng): Eval plan: holdout set of ~600 prompts (200 per flow). Metrics: precision/recall for extraction, ROUGE/EM for summaries, hallucination flag count, token-cost per request, latency p50/p95. We should wire these into Redwood Console dashboards for ongoing regression monitoring.

Anya (Solutions Eng): I will upload the prompt inventory to the shared sheet: https://docs.example.com/acme-poc-prompts and create the eval harness repo `acme-poc-evals` with a starter script to run baseline against dev-gpu. Snippet for harness run: `python run_evals.py --model redwood-open-7b-q --seed 42 --out results.json`.

Priya (SalesEng): Timeline proposal: Week 1 = prompt inventory + security Q + decide hosting; Week 2 = baseline runs + perf SLO validation; Week 3 = tuning + rerun evals; Week 4 = customer acceptance demo and handoff. Need Acme confirmation on that schedule.

Marisa (AE): Thanks all. I’ll sync with Acme PM and update this thread with the questionnaire and hosting choice. @deploy-bot can you reserve a dev GPU slot for baseline runs next Tue morning?

deploy-bot: Scheduled — `dev-gpu-3` reserved Tue 10:00–14:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Sam (Eng): One more blocker: we need PII-scrubbed sample data or synthetic equivalents. If Acme can't provide scrubbed samples, we'll provision synthetic generator and note potential eval variance.

Marisa (AE): Noted — I’ll ask for scrubbed samples and fallback permission for synthetic data. Will update by EOD. :thumbsup:
